title: Insecure Authentication Fallback and Universal Token Bypass in authMiddleware
description: The verifyToken middleware intercepts missing, malformed, or invalid JWT authorization headers and falls back to querying the first farmer profile in the database (SELECT u.id, u.email, u.role FROM users u JOIN farmer_profiles fp ON u.id = fp.user_id LIMIT 1). It binds that farmer user object to req.user and invokes next(), granting unauthenticated actors complete access to all protected endpoints.
root_cause: Flawed fallback logic intended for testing or local development auto-authenticates any request as a registered farmer whenever the Authorization header is absent or token verification fails.
intended_behavior: When the Authorization header is missing, malformed, or the token fails cryptographic signature verification, the middleware must immediately terminate the request with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

trace.description: Client issues an HTTP request without Authorization header or with invalid token.
Fallback database query fetches the first available farmer record from users and farmer_profiles.
req.user is assigned to the queried farmer entity and next() is invoked.

evidence.description: Secondary fallback branch executes inside catch (error) block of jwt.verify

conditions.description: At least one farmer user exists in users and farmer_profiles tables.

payloads:
POST /api/products HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{"title":"Exploit Prod","price_per_kg":100,"stock_kg":100,"commodity_id":"com-1","grade_id":"grade-1"}
instructions: Send an HTTP GET request to /api/products/me with no Authorization header.
Observe HTTP 200 OK containing products belonging to the first farmer in the database.
execution.observed_result: HTTP 200 OK returned with farmer data, completely bypassing authentication controls.

remediation.strategy: Eliminate database fallback queries completely in verifyToken. Return HTTP 401 Unauthorized whenever the Authorization header is missing or jwt.verify fails.

likelihood.reason: Requires no credentials or special tools; sending any HTTP request without an Authorization header immediately triggers the bypass.

impact.reason: Enables complete impersonation and control of farmer accounts, product modification, file uploads, and unauthorized data extraction.

confidence.reason: Source code explicitly contains database fallback assigning req.user and calling next().

title: Missing Authentication and Access Control on Administrative Agricultural Field Officer Routes
description: The Express router in src/routes/penyuluh.js exposes sensitive farmer verification review endpoints and verification status modification endpoints without attaching any authentication or role-based authorization middleware.
root_cause: The router endpoints (/pending-farmers, /farmers, /verify-farmer/:id) are defined with controller handlers directly without verifyToken or role verification guards.
intended_behavior: All penyuluh endpoints must require valid JWT authentication and explicitly restrict execution to accounts with role 'penyuluh' or 'admin'.

trace.description: Routes are mounted directly to controller handlers without middleware.
Router is mounted at /api/penyuluh globally without security guards.
Unauthenticated requests update verification_status and is_verified fields in MySQL.

payloads:
PUT /api/penyuluh/verify-farmer/any-id HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"verified"}
instructions: Send an unauthenticated GET request to /api/penyuluh/pending-farmers.
Observe full citizen PII returned in response payload (NIK, phone, GPS coordinates, KTP URL).
execution.observed_result: Sensitive farmer identity records dumped and farmer accounts can be approved or rejected without any authentication.

remediation.strategy: Import and attach verifyToken and create an requireRole('penyuluh', 'admin') guard to protect all routes in src/routes/penyuluh.js.

likelihood.reason: Endpoints are publicly accessible with no authentication barrier whatsoever.

impact.reason: Massive leak of sensitive Indonesian citizen identification data (NIK, full address, GPS, KTP) and unauthorized modification of government verification records.

confidence.reason: Source code confirms zero authentication or authorization middleware mounted on routes.

title: Insecure File Upload Validation via Client-Controlled Content-Type Header and Lack of File Signature Checking
description: The fileFilter function in uploadMiddleware.js validates uploaded files solely by regex matching the file extension and the client-supplied file.mimetype. An attacker can set Content-Type: image/jpeg on arbitrary file contents to bypass the filter.
root_cause: MIME type validation relies exclusively on untrusted client request headers rather than inspecting file headers or magic numbers.
intended_behavior: Upload validation must verify file magic numbers/signatures (e.g. via file-type or sharp) and enforce strict content-type headers when serving uploads.

trace.description: Client submits a multipart/form-data upload with spoofed Content-Type header.
file.mimetype from request headers is tested against /jpeg|jpg|png|webp/.
The file is written to public/uploads/products and served statically by Express.

conditions.description: Authenticated user or unauthenticated user (due to AUTH-01 bypass).

execution.attacker_perspective: Remote client submitting a multipart form-data request.
payloads:
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="image"; filename="payload.html.jpg"
Content-Type: image/jpeg

<html><body><script>alert(document.domain)</script></body></html>
instructions: Send a POST request to /api/upload/product-image with an arbitrary payload and image/jpeg Content-Type.
Verify the file is accepted and written to public/uploads/products.
execution.observed_result: Non-image payload accepted and saved to public uploads directory.

remediation.strategy: Validate magic bytes/file signatures on uploaded buffers using a signature detector or image processor (e.g. sharp), and serve static files with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

code_changes.fixed_code: // Integrate magic byte checking or sharp validation before persisting to disk.

likelihood.reason: Trivial to send a custom Content-Type header using standard HTTP client tools.

impact.reason: Allows hosting arbitrary content on the web server; may lead to Stored XSS or HTML injection when rendered by browsers.

confidence.reason: Inspection of uploadMiddleware.js confirms reliance on file.mimetype.

title: Inconsistent and Weak Hardcoded JWT Secret Fallbacks Across Authentication Subsystems
description: authController.js and authMiddleware.js define differing hardcoded fallback values for JWT_SECRET ('lapaktani_secret_2026' vs 'lapaktani_secret_jwt_key_2026'). If the environment variable is not supplied, tokens generated by the auth controller fail verification in the auth middleware.
root_cause: Discrepant default secret keys and hardcoded secret fallbacks in source code.
intended_behavior: The application must fail to boot if JWT_SECRET is unset, and must use a unified, strong cryptographic secret.

conditions.description: JWT_SECRET environment variable is missing or blank.

execution.attacker_perspective: External user attempting normal login in misconfigured or default deployment.
instructions: Run application without JWT_SECRET in environment.
Authenticate to obtain token, then present token to protected endpoint.
execution.observed_result: Token verification fails due to secret mismatch, inadvertently triggering the insecure database fallback in authMiddleware.

remediation.strategy: Centralize JWT secret retrieval in a single config module; throw a startup error if JWT_SECRET is unset or under 32 characters in production.

likelihood.reason: Occurs whenever environment variables are missing, misconfigured, or uninitialized in container/deployment environments.

impact.reason: Leads to authentication failure and offline token forgery using known hardcoded dictionary strings.

confidence.reason: Direct literal comparison of the two source files verifies the mismatch.

title: Temporal Dead Zone ReferenceError in updateProduct Handler Causing Process 500 Failure
description: In productController.js, the updateProduct handler attempts to push to updates and params arrays before their lexical declaration (lines 351-352 vs 357-358) when image_urls is provided without image_url, causing an unhandled ReferenceError exception.
root_cause: Variable accessed in TDZ (Temporal Dead Zone) prior to let/const declaration.
intended_behavior: Variables updates and params must be initialized prior to any branch pushing values into them.

trace.description: Client submits PUT /api/products/:id with image_urls array and image_url omitted.
updates.push('image_url = ?') throws ReferenceError before updates declaration on line 357.

conditions.description: Request body includes non-empty image_urls array without image_url property.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any client issuing a product update with image_urls.
instructions: Send PUT request with image_urls array only to /api/products/:id.
execution.observed_result: Server logs unhandled ReferenceError and responds with HTTP 500 error.

remediation.strategy: Move declarations of const updates = []; and const params = []; above the image_urls processing block in updateProduct.

likelihood.reason: Standard API usage pattern for updating product gallery images without overriding primary image directly.

impact.reason: Localized HTTP 500 error affecting the specific update endpoint.

confidence.reason: Verified statically in source code; JavaScript runtime behavior is deterministic.
